sourceFitAssessment.learnerTask: See normal topoisomerase cut/reseal versus a stabilized cleavage complex
sourceFitAssessment.gap: Verbal repair-worker analogy lacks before/after DNA-enzyme geometry
sourceFitAssessment.accuracyGuardrails: Do not depict simply switching enzyme off; multiple mechanisms; no efficacy/cardiac-risk prediction
sourceFitAssessment.reasoning: The upper scene starts with joined double-stranded DNA, shows an enzyme-held cut and passing segment, then joined strands again; the lower scene retains cut ends within an enzyme-associated complex with drug. This teaches stabilization of the cleavage intermediate rather than a simple switch-off. The article identifies this as one doxorubicin mechanism and preserves intercalation/reactive-molecule context and normal-cell effects. Cumulative/delayed cardiac risk is supported separately by the explicitly dated FDA label. Neither diagram geometry nor the fictional DNA-break/baseline-heart-imaging example predicts efficacy or absence of later heart injury.
